project.name: dandori
project.description: Dandori is a meal-planning co-pilot for a few invited users cooking for themselves: it plans batch-cooked meals, tracks kitchen inventory, adapts to schedule changes and fills an online supermarket cart. Built in Go with templ, htmx, PostgreSQL/pgvector and Claude.

nodes.name: main.go
nodes.summary: Single-binary entry point for Dandori: `serve` reads DANDORI_* and Anthropic settings from the environment, wires telemetry, the Claude or demo LLM and Supabase auth into the app, then serves HTTP with graceful shutdown; `healthcheck` probes /healthz for the container.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Dispatches the `serve` or `healthcheck` subcommand: builds app.Config from the environment, picks the demo or Claude LLM, validates required settings and sets up telemetry with a flush on exit.

nodes.name: serve
nodes.summary: Starts the app and its scheduler, listens on addr and serves HTTP until the context ends, then shuts the server down gracefully.

nodes.name: healthcheck
nodes.summary: healthcheck fails unless the app on addr answers its health check with 200: serving, with its database reachable.

nodes.name: agent.go
nodes.summary: Defines the agent package's model-facing vocabulary for the hand-written tool-use loop (ADR-0003): the LLM port, requests, responses, token usage, messages, content blocks, tool specs and the retryable-error marker.
nodes.languageNotes: Go interfaces are satisfied implicitly: anthropic.LLM, fakellm.LLM and recipes.DemoLLM all implement the LLM port without declaring it.

nodes.name: LLM
nodes.summary: LLM is the port to the language model: send the conversation and the tools, get the model's next turn.

nodes.name: Request
nodes.summary: Request is one call to the model.

nodes.name: Response
nodes.summary: Response is the model's turn.

nodes.name: Usage
nodes.summary: Usage is the tokens a model turn used. Thinking is counted in Output; CacheRead and CacheWrite are the input tokens read from and written to the prompt cache.

nodes.name: Message
nodes.summary: Message is one turn of the conversation.

nodes.name: Block
nodes.summary: Block is one piece of a Message.

nodes.name: ToolSpec
nodes.summary: ToolSpec describes a tool to the model.

nodes.name: RetryableError
nodes.summary: RetryableError marks an LLM failure worth retrying, such as a rate limit or an overloaded server. After is how long the server asked us to wait.

nodes.name: anthropic.go
nodes.summary: Claude API adapter implementing the agent LLM port over the Beta Messages endpoint, with server-side refusal fallback, prompt-cache breakpoints, effort settings, OpenTelemetry span attributes and classification of retryable failures (the SDK itself never retries).

nodes.name: LLM
nodes.summary: LLM sends requests to Claude.

nodes.name: New
nodes.summary: New returns the Claude LLM. Credentials come from the environment (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, or a profile from `ant auth login`).

nodes.name: Send
nodes.summary: Send implements agent.LLM. It goes through the Beta Messages endpoint for the server-side refusal fallback.

nodes.name: toolParam
nodes.summary: Converts an agent ToolSpec into the SDK's Beta tool parameter with its JSON input schema.

nodes.name: messageParam
nodes.summary: Converts an agent Message into the SDK's Beta message parameter, block by block.

nodes.name: blockParam
nodes.summary: Converts an agent content Block to the SDK's form, replaying the model's own raw blocks unchanged and building text, tool-use and tool-result blocks otherwise.

nodes.name: classify
nodes.summary: classify marks the failures worth retrying: rate limits, timeouts, overloaded or failing servers, and the network.

nodes.name: brief.go
nodes.summary: Defines Brief, what the agent is told for one Run (cached system prompt, per-user prompt, effort, tools, end-of-turn check), and Tool, an action the model may call.

nodes.name: Brief
nodes.summary: Brief is what the agent is told for one Run and the tools it may use. Each kind of Run builds its own.

nodes.name: Tool
nodes.summary: Tool is something the agent can do. Run's result goes back to the model; an error goes back as a failed tool result, so the model can recover, unless it is a *Failure, which fails the Run.

nodes.name: fakellm.go
nodes.summary: Scripted fake LLM for tests: each model request is answered by the next scripted Step (reply, tool calls, failure, overload, hang, delayed answers), recording every request so Runs are deterministic.

nodes.name: LLM
nodes.summary: LLM answers requests from its script, in order. It is safe to script more steps while a Run is using it.

nodes.name: Step
nodes.summary: Step is one scripted answer of the model.

nodes.name: Call
nodes.summary: Call is one tool call the model makes.

nodes.name: New
nodes.summary: New returns a fake LLM that answers with steps.

nodes.name: Script
nodes.summary: Script adds steps to the end of the script.

nodes.name: Requests
nodes.summary: Requests returns every request the model was sent, in order.

nodes.name: Reply
nodes.summary: Reply ends the model's turn with text.

nodes.name: CallTools
nodes.summary: CallTools has the model call tools, saying text first if it isn't empty.

nodes.name: CallTool
nodes.summary: CallTool has the model call one tool.

nodes.name: Respond
nodes.summary: Respond answers with resp as given, e.g. to script an unusual stop reason.

nodes.name: Then
nodes.summary: Then answers with the step next makes from the request, as a model reads what its tools returned, such as the id of what one stored.

nodes.name: Fail
nodes.summary: Fail makes the request fail with err.

nodes.name: Overloaded
nodes.summary: Overloaded makes the request fail in a way worth retrying.

nodes.name: Hang
nodes.summary: Hang never answers: the request blocks until its context is cancelled.

nodes.name: After
nodes.summary: After holds the answer back until ch is closed, so a test can act while the model is "thinking".

nodes.name: Wait
nodes.summary: Wait has the model take d to answer, as a real one does.

nodes.name: Send
nodes.summary: Send implements agent.LLM.

nodes.name: loop.go
nodes.summary: The agent's tool-use loop: Loop.Run sends a Brief to the model, runs requested tools, retries retryable failures with exponential backoff, bounds turns, and emits every step as a Trace Event until the model ends its turn.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Go 1.26's generic errors.AsType to unwrap *RetryableError and *Failure without a pre-declared target variable.

nodes.name: Loop
nodes.summary: Runs Briefs against the model, configured with the LLM, model name, retry count, backoff and a maximum number of turns per Run.

nodes.name: Run
nodes.summary: Run carries out b, emitting every step to tr, until the model ends its turn without calling a tool. It fails with a *Failure, or ctx's error once ctx is cancelled.

nodes.name: send
nodes.summary: send asks the model, retrying failures worth retrying with a growing wait.

nodes.name: runTools
nodes.summary: runTools runs the tool calls of the model's turn, in order, and returns their results. A failing tool is reported to the model, not fatal, unless it fails with a *Failure, which fails the Run.

nodes.name: trace.go
nodes.summary: Defines a Run's Trace vocabulary: the Trace Event kinds and payload, the Trace sink interface, failure Reasons and the Failure error type that ends a Run.

nodes.name: TraceEvent
nodes.summary: TraceEvent is one Trace Event of a Run: its kind and data.

nodes.name: Trace
nodes.summary: Trace receives a Run's Trace Events as they happen. Emit must work after the Run's context is cancelled, so a cancellation can still be recorded.

nodes.name: Failure
nodes.summary: Failure is a Run failing for Reason, Detail saying more, verbatim, when there is more.

nodes.name: TestTheIngredientsSheetAddsInPlace
nodes.summary: Posted from the side sheet by htmx, the add form answers with the sheet's body alone: the add confirmed and the form cleared, or refused with what was typed.

nodes.name: TestEachUserHasTheirOwnIngredients
nodes.summary: One User never sees another's Ingredients, and may add the same food.

nodes.name: TestANearMissSuggestsTheIngredientItMeant
nodes.summary: A name close to an Ingredient's, which doesn't normalise to it, suggests that one. The User picks it, adding nothing and finding it in the list, or confirms the name they typed and adds it.

nodes.name: TestTheIngredientsSheetSuggestsInPlace
nodes.summary: The suggestion, picking it and confirming the name typed each answer with the side sheet's body alone when htmx posts them. Picking a name the User has no Ingredient of confirms nothing.

nodes.name: TestANameIsSuggestedForOnLeavingIt
nodes.summary: Leaving the name asks for a suggestion before the form is sent: the one it may have meant, carrying the name's confirmation, or nothing for another food, a blank name, or a name the User has, which adding refuses.

nodes.name: TestSearchingIngredientsBySpelling
nodes.summary: A search ranks the Ingredients by spelling, the most alike first, so a typo still finds the Ingredient; one that finds nothing says so, and a blank one lists them all.

nodes.name: TestEditingAnIngredient
nodes.summary: An Ingredient is edited in place: its name, its nutritional values, fibre and sugar becoming unknown, and its usual Storage Location, at any time.

nodes.name: TestARenameToAnotherIngredientIsRefused
nodes.summary: A rename that normalises to another Ingredient's name is refused on the name, naming that one; renaming to the Ingredient's own name in other words is not. A new name only close to another's suggests it, and saving it again confirms the name typed.

nodes.name: TestTheUnitIsFixedOnceStockIsCounted
nodes.summary: The unit changes while no Movement refers to the Ingredient. Once one does, it is refused on the unit, saying the Movements are recorded in it, even with the Stock Item counted to nothing; the rest of the edit is not saved either.

nodes.name: TestEditingAnIngredientLeavesTheKitchenAsItWas
nodes.summary: Editing nutrition, or renaming, changes no Movement: the Kitchen page holds what it held, under the new name.

nodes.name: TestDeletingAnIngredient
nodes.summary: An Ingredient nothing refers to is deleted. One with a Movement is refused, saying why, and the database refuses it as well.

nodes.name: TestTheIngredientsSheetEditsAndDeletesInPlace
nodes.summary: Posted from the side sheet by htmx, editing and deleting answer with the sheet's body alone, searched as it was: confirmed with the row closed, or refused with the row open as typed and why.

nodes.name: TestDeletingAnIngredientAsksFirst
nodes.summary: Deleting an Ingredient asks once, in the User's Language, naming it, from a step its row's Delete opens; the row has no Delete that posts at once.

nodes.name: TestAnotherUsersIngredientCantBeEditedOrDeleted
nodes.summary: A User can neither edit nor delete another's Ingredient.

nodes.name: TestBrowserEditsAndDeletesInTheSideSheet
nodes.summary: In the side sheet, an Ingredient's row opens to edit it, and saving closes it in place, the sheet staying open; a refused delete keeps it open with why, and a delete, asked once in a sheet over it, takes the Ingredient off the list.

nodes.name: TestTheIngredientsSheetRefusesAndConfirmsEditsInPlace
nodes.summary: Posted by htmx, the edits a plain post makes answer in place too: a value required, a rename to another Ingredient refused and one close to another suggested, then confirmed; the unit changed while nothing refers to the Ingredient; fibre and sugar made unknown; and the Kitchen page holding what it held.

nodes.name: kitchen_test.go
nodes.summary: Seam-1 tests for the Kitchen page and scheduler: a new kitchen's guidance, beats bringing every user's kitchen up to now, isolating one user's failure, and idempotent re-runs of a step.

nodes.name: TestANewKitchenPageSaysHowToStart
nodes.summary: The Kitchen page tells a new kitchen how to start, and opens the Ingredients from the page's header.

nodes.name: TestTheSchedulerBringsEveryUsersKitchenUpToNow
nodes.summary: The scheduler beats every five minutes on the clock and brings every User's kitchen up to now, whether or not they have a page open: each one's Today shows the last beat, which a page opened in between leaves as it was.

nodes.name: TestABeatFailingForOneUserStillBringsTheOthersUpToNow
nodes.summary: A beat that fails for one User still brings the others up to now, and the failure is logged. The User it failed for sees the last beat that didn't, with its day.

nodes.name: TestTheStepRunAgainForTheSameMomentChangesNothing
nodes.summary: Running the step again for the moment a beat brought the kitchen to changes nothing: a page opened then, which runs it first, writes nothing to the kitchen and shows the beat as it was.

nodes.name: language_test.go
nodes.summary: Seam-1 and browser tests for a user's Language: chosen at first sign-in, changeable on the Profile until a Food Term or running parse fixes it, per-user, pre-sign-in Italian switch, refusals, and the page lang attribute.

nodes.name: TestTheFirstSignInAsksForTheLanguage
nodes.summary: A User's first sign-in asks for their Language before anything else. Picking Italian makes the pages Italian, and the next sign-in doesn't ask again.

nodes.name: TestTheLanguageCanBeChangedOnTheProfile
nodes.summary: The Language can be changed on the Profile, while the User has written no Food Term, confirmed in the Language chosen.

nodes.name: TestEachUserHasTheirOwnLanguage
nodes.summary: Each User has their own Language.

nodes.name: TestPagesBeforeSignInSwitchToItalian
nodes.summary: Pages before signing in are in English, with a switch to Italian that the following pages remember, up to the Language choice.

nodes.name: TestTheLanguageChoiceRefusesAnotherLanguage
nodes.summary: A Language Dandori doesn't speak is refused, with the choice asked again.

nodes.name: TestTheProfileRefusesAnotherLanguageKeepingTheUsers
nodes.summary: A change the Profile refuses comes back with the Language as it was.

nodes.name: TestTheLanguageIsChosenOnce
nodes.summary: The Language is chosen once at the first sign-in: the choice, posted again, goes to Today and changes nothing; changing it is the Profile's.

nodes.name: TestTheLanguageStaysOnceTheUserHasAnIngredient
nodes.summary: Once the User has added an Ingredient, their Language stays: the Profile refuses a change, keeping the one they have.

nodes.name: TestTheLanguageCantChangeWhileAParseRunIsGoing
nodes.summary: The Language can't change while a parse Run is going, so its Recipe Draft can't arrive in the one just left; once the Run ends with no Food Term written, it can again.

nodes.name: TestTheLanguageSwitchStaysOnThisSite
nodes.summary: The Language switch opens a page of this site again, whatever slashes its path begins with: a browser reads a location beginning with // as another site's.

nodes.name: TestBrowserKeepsThePageLangInStepWithTheLanguage
nodes.summary: A boosted change of Language leaves the page's lang the new Language's, which a screen reader reads it by, and the page stays closed to a browser's own translation.

nodes.name: look_test.go
nodes.summary: Seam-1 and browser tests for visual conventions: pages numbering their own groups, titles setting data in the body face, and the slim sky strip on every page but Today.

nodes.name: TestAPageNumbersItsOwnGroups
nodes.summary: A page numbers its own groups: the Recipe Library, a Recipe, a Run and the Ingredients page. The square is for a side sheet's, such as the Ingredients sheet's.

nodes.name: TestATitleSetsItsDataInTheBodyFace
nodes.summary: A title sets its times, quantities and User text in the body face, where l, I and 1 are told apart: Today's time of day, a Recipe's name.

nodes.name: TestBrowserTheSkyIsSlimOnEveryPageButToday
nodes.summary: On a phone the full sky is Today's: every other page has a slim strip of it, so its first content, after the page's header, sits within 300px of the top.

nodes.name: measure
nodes.summary: measure is the number script works out on b's page.

nodes.name: meal_out_test.go
nodes.summary: Seam-1 tests for the Profile's Meal Out estimate: defaults, saving with unknown fibre and sugar, per-field refusals, htmx fragment answers and per-user isolation.

nodes.name: TestANewUserHasTheDefaultMealOutEstimate
nodes.summary: A new User's Profile shows the default Meal Out estimate.

nodes.name: TestTheMealOutEstimateIsSavedWithFibreAndSugarGivenOrUnknown
nodes.summary: A saved Meal Out estimate is shown back, and fibre and sugar left blank stay unknown, never 0.

nodes.name: TestARefusedMealOutValueIsRefusedOnItsField
nodes.summary: A required value missing or negative, or a value not whole, is refused on its field, saving nothing, with what was typed kept.

nodes.name: TestTheMealOutSectionAnswersHTMXWithItself
nodes.summary: Posted by htmx, the Meal Out section answers with itself: saved with a Notice, or refused as typed.

nodes.name: TestEachUserHasTheirOwnMealOutEstimate
nodes.summary: Each User sees only their own Meal Out estimate.

nodes.name: move_test.go
nodes.summary: Seam-1 and browser tests for moving stock between Storage Locations: partial and full moves, refusals, count-first flows, stale forms, Italian, htmx posts and ordering behind other movements.

nodes.name: TestMovingStockBetweenStorageLocations
nodes.summary: Moving part of a Stock Item leaves the rest and adds to the other Storage Location's, the Stock Item it makes there if none was. Moving all of it removes the source, whose Movements stay.

nodes.name: TestAMoveStartsFromAllOfTheStockItem
nodes.summary: The form starts from all of the Stock Item, in its unit, and leaves the target to the User, offering the two other Storage Locations with what Dandori believes they hold.

nodes.name: TestMovingPartOfAPiece
nodes.summary: A quantity follows its unit's rules: pieces have one decimal place.

nodes.name: TestARefusedMove
nodes.summary: A move is refused on the field, keeping what was typed and leaving the kitchen as it was.

nodes.name: TestCountingFirstLetsAMoveThrough
nodes.summary: When Dandori holds too little, the User counts first and the same move then goes through.

nodes.name: TestAMoveNeedsAnotherStorageLocation
nodes.summary: A move needs a target, which is another Storage Location.

nodes.name: TestAMoveFromAnOldFormIsChecked
nodes.summary: A move is checked against the Kitchen Ledger as it stands, not as the form showed it.

nodes.name: TestAMoveIsNotACount
nodes.summary: The Kitchen page says when a Stock Item was counted, which a move doesn't change: stock only moved somewhere was never counted there, and says nothing.

nodes.name: TestACountStartsFromWhatAMoveLeft
nodes.summary: A Count of stock moved in starts from what the move left there.

nodes.name: TestMoveOfNoStockItem
nodes.summary: A Stock Item holding nothing can't be moved, and neither can another User's. A post for a Storage Location that isn't one is no move at all.

nodes.name: TestMovesInItalian
nodes.summary: A move's cause speaks the User's Language, each Storage Location with its own preposition.

nodes.name: TestAMovePostedAsHTMX
nodes.summary: As htmx posts it, the form answers with a fragment: the move confirmed in a floating Notice alone, closing the sheet and telling the page to list its stock again, or the form itself as typed with why it was refused, confirming nothing.

nodes.name: TestBrowserMovesStockInPlace
nodes.summary: A move from a row happens in its sheet: once saved the sheet closes, the list shows both Stock Items, and a floating Notice says what moved. A refused one keeps the sheet open on the field, confirming nothing.

nodes.name: TestAMoveHappensAfterTheMovementItWaitedBehind
nodes.summary: A move that waited behind a later Movement happens after it, so its Stock Items' Movements end on what the Kitchen page shows.

nodes.name: movements_test.go
nodes.summary: Seam-1 and browser tests for a Stock Item's Movements history: why it holds what it does, corrections by recount, per-item history, links from the Count form, empty locations, years, Italian, and the sheet fragment.

nodes.name: TestAStockItemsMovementsTellWhyItHoldsWhatItDoes
nodes.summary: A Stock Item's Movements answer why it holds what it does: newest first, each with when it happened, its cause, what Dandori believed before and after, and the User's note.

nodes.name: TestAMistakeIsCorrectedByAnotherCount
nodes.summary: A mistaken Count is corrected by another Count, and both stay: the Movements offer no way to change or remove one. A Count that changes nothing is one of them too.

nodes.name: TestEachStockItemHasItsOwnMovements
nodes.summary: A Stock Item is one Ingredient in one Storage Location: its Movements are its own.

nodes.name: TestAStockItemAtNothingKeepsItsMovements
nodes.summary: A Stock Item counted to nothing leaves the Kitchen page but keeps its Movements, which its Ingredient's Count form reaches, in whichever Storage Location it was.

nodes.name: TestACountFormHasOneMovementsLink
nodes.summary: The Count form has one Movements link and one Choose another, whatever Movements its Ingredient has. Without htmx the link opens the Storage Location the form started on.

nodes.name: TestAStorageLocationWithNoMovementsSaysSo
nodes.summary: A Storage Location with no Movements of an Ingredient the User has says so, as a page and in the sheet. A Staple is such an Ingredient, though no Stock Item holds it.

nodes.name: TestMovementsLinkEveryStorageLocation
nodes.summary: The Movements link all three Storage Locations, the current one marked, so without htmx each stays reachable and a move can be followed from one side to the other.

nodes.name: TestMovementsOfNoStockItem
nodes.summary: Only an Ingredient the User has, in a Storage Location, is there to open.

nodes.name: TestAMovementOfAnotherYearShowsItsYear
nodes.summary: A Movement of another year says so; one of this year has no need to.

nodes.name: TestMovementsInItalian
nodes.summary: The Movements speak the User's Language, whatever the Language of their note.

nodes.name: TestStorageLocationsInItalian
nodes.summary: A Count's confirmation says "in" or "nel" as each Storage Location takes it.

nodes.name: TestTheMovementsSheetIsAFragment
nodes.summary: As htmx asks for them, the Movements are the sheet's body alone.

nodes.name: TestBrowserOpensAStockItemsMovementsInPlace
nodes.summary: Opening a Stock Item shows its Movements in the side sheet, newest first, leaving the User where they are on the Kitchen page; a Count form opens them over its sheet.

nodes.name: TestBrowserCountFormHoldsItsLayoutOnAPhoneInItalian
nodes.summary: On a phone, in Italian, the Count form keeps Choose another beside the Ingredient's name, and Movements across from the Count button, without overflowing the sheet.

nodes.name: notice_test.go
nodes.summary: Browser tests for floating Notices: shown without JavaScript, readable over the Count sheet on a phone with the keyboard up, and keeping their timer as the sheet closes.

nodes.name: TestBrowserANoticeShowsWithoutJS
nodes.summary: With no script, a plain post still lands on a page whose floating Notice shows: the Profile saved, and a Count from its own page.

nodes.name: TestBrowserANoticeOnAPhoneWithTheKeyboardUp
nodes.summary: On a phone with the keyboard up, a Count's floating Notice shows whole at the top of the screen, over the Count sheet, its Close a full touch target that, focused, has the ring a navy ground needs.

nodes.name: TestBrowserANoticeKeepsItsTimeAsTheSheetCloses
nodes.summary: A floating Notice keeps its time as the sheet it shows over closes, from a tap outside it: it doesn't start again.

nodes.name: parse_test.go
nodes.summary: Seam-1 and browser tests for recipe parse Runs driven by the fake LLM: pasted recipes becoming Recipe Drafts, refusals, retries, turn limits, tool-result feedback loops, language handling, the system prompt and tool schema, trace rendering, concurrency, isolation and the demo LLM.
nodes.languageNotes: Tests live in package app_test (external test package), so they exercise the app only through its exported HTTP surface.

nodes.name: submittedLasagne
nodes.summary: submittedLasagne is what the model submits for pastedLasagne: rice is known, the rest is new.

nodes.name: TestAPastedRecipeBecomesARecipeDraftThroughARun
nodes.summary: A pasted recipe is read by a parse Run, whose page shows its Trace, into a Recipe Draft showing what the model submitted: the known rice in its own unit, and each new Ingredient's proposed values, fibre and sugar unknown where the model couldn't tell.

nodes.name: TestARefusedPasteFailsItsRunSayingWhy
nodes.summary: A refusal that stands after the fallback fails the Run, saying why the model refused.

nodes.name: TestAPasteThatIsNotARecipeFailsItsRunWithTheModelsReason
nodes.summary: A model that ends its turn without submitting a Recipe fails the Run, its last message as the reason, and no Recipe Draft is offered.

nodes.name: TestTryAgainOnAFailedParseRunStartsANewOneWithTheSameText
nodes.summary: "Try again" on a failed parse Run starts a new one with the same text, without pasting it again; a Run that succeeded doesn't offer it.

nodes.name: TestAPasteOver20000CharactersIsRefusedOnItsField
nodes.summary: A paste over 20,000 characters, counted after trimming, is refused on its field with the limit stated, keeping the text, and starts no Run; one of exactly 20,000 is read.

nodes.name: TestAModelFailureWorthRetryingShowsInTheTraceAndTheRunSucceeds
nodes.summary: A model failure worth retrying is retried, the retry shown in the Trace, and the Run still succeeds.

nodes.name: TestARunPastTheTurnLimitFailsSayingSo
nodes.summary: A model that keeps calling tools fails its Run once it reaches the turn limit.

nodes.name: TestSubmitRecipesProblemsGoBackToTheModelWhichFixesThem
nodes.summary: What submit_recipe can't take goes back to the model, said so it can fix it: here the known rice in millilitres, and a new Ingredient without its values. The model fixes both, and the Recipe Draft is what it submitted second.

nodes.name: TestUnknownKindsGoBackToTheModelAllAtOnce
nodes.summary: Every kind of appliance and of Slot not on its list goes back to the model in one refusal, so it fixes them all in one call and the Recipe Draft holds only kinds.

nodes.name: italianLasagne
nodes.summary: italianLasagne is what the model submits for pastedLasagne in Italian.

nodes.name: TestARecipeInAnotherLanguageBecomesARecipeDraftInTheUsersLanguage
nodes.summary: The parse Run's system prompt names the User's Language, so a recipe pasted in English by a User speaking Italian becomes a Recipe Draft in Italian.

nodes.name: TestTheParseSystemPromptVariesOnlyByLanguage
nodes.summary: The system prompt is the same for every User and paste of one Language, so it is cached; what varies, the User's known Ingredients and the pasted text, comes after it.

nodes.name: TestSubmitRecipesSchemaStatesTheRulesItChecks
nodes.summary: submit_recipe's schema tells the model the rules its checks hold a Recipe to, so a typical one is taken the first time rather than refused: the kinds of appliance, a quantity whole but for a piece's, and nutritional values to one decimal place, none negative or too large.

nodes.name: TestATracesFixedLinesAreInTheUsersLanguageAndTheModelsTextVerbatim
nodes.summary: A Trace's fixed lines are plain words in the User's Language, whichever it is when they look, timed to the minute, each folding its data, the model's and the tool's names included; what the model said is as it said it.

nodes.name: TestSeveralParseRunsGoAtOnceEachMakingItsOwnRecipeDraft
nodes.summary: Several parse Runs can go at once, each making its own Recipe Draft: both are asking the model before either is answered.

nodes.name: TestTwoUsersNeverSeeEachOthersRunsOrRecipeDrafts
nodes.summary: A User sees neither another's Runs, their streams nor their Recipe Drafts, and can't cancel their Runs.

nodes.name: TestARecipeDraftShowsOnlyOnceItsRunHasEnded
nodes.summary: A Recipe Draft shows only once its parse Run has ended, since the model may still change it.

nodes.name: pastesInTheSheet
nodes.summary: pastesInTheSheet pastes text in the sheet the Recipe Library's + opens, focused on its field, and reads it.

nodes.name: TestBrowserAPasteRefusedInTheSheetStaysInIt
nodes.summary: A paste refused in the sheet stays in it, saying why with its field focused, over the Recipe Library.

nodes.name: TestBrowserARunsInputAndTraceDataAreFoldedUntilOpened
nodes.summary: A Run's page folds what the User gave it, the paste, at its top, and its Trace reads as a list of timestamped lines: what the model was sent and what it and its tools said is folded under each, closed until the User opens it.

nodes.name: demoKitchen
nodes.summary: demoKitchen signs a new User in, speaking the Language named language, on an app whose Runs ask the demo model mise run dev uses.

nodes.name: TestTheDemoLLMReadsAnyPasteIntoARecipeDraft
nodes.summary: The demo model makes a Recipe Draft of any paste without a real model: named after its first line, and taking an Ingredient the User knows in the unit they know it in.

nodes.name: TestTheDemoLLMWritesInTheUsersLanguage
nodes.summary: The demo model writes in the Language the system prompt names.

nodes.name: planning_test.go
nodes.summary: Seam-1 and browser tests for planning a Cycle into a pending Plan Proposal: what the planner is told (profile, library, brief, kitchen, language), plan hard-rule checks, failing runs, one planning run at a time, per-user isolation, cancellation and storage failures.

nodes.name: idIn
nodes.summary: idIn is the id the pattern's group finds in the prompt of the first request of the Run req belongs to.

nodes.name: fridayDraft
nodes.summary: fridayDraft is a draft Plan of friday, read from the prompt of req: yogurt at breakfast, a Rice bowl prepared at lunch for three Portions at 1.25×, eaten at lunch and dinner with the third frozen, and a Portion of lasagne at the snack.

nodes.name: TestPlanningACycleEndsInAPendingPlanProposal
nodes.summary: Opening a Cycle lands on the Kitchen Check, listing what the kitchen holds with a Count for each; its button starts a planning Run whose Trace shows, and which ends in a pending Plan Proposal at the top of the Cycle page: each Slot with its Portion, each Prep Session with its Portions' size, its Ingredients scaled, its minutes and where each Portion goes, and the planner's summary.

nodes.name: plansFriday
nodes.summary: plansFriday opens friday and plans it, through the Kitchen Check, into a pending Plan Proposal of fridayDraft summed up as summary.

nodes.name: TestACountOnTheKitchenCheckIsWhatThePlannerIsTold
nodes.summary: A Count made on the Kitchen Check is what the planner is told the kitchen holds.

nodes.name: TestThePlannerIsToldTheProfileTheLibraryTheBriefTheKitchenAndTheLanguage
nodes.summary: The planner is told the Profile, the Recipe Library, the Ingredients, the Planning Brief, what the kitchen holds and the User's Language; its system prompt names no Language, so it is the same for everyone.

nodes.name: TestThePlannerIsToldTheLowCareBriefAndTheLanguage
nodes.summary: An empty Planning Brief is told as its low-care default, and an Italian User's planner is told their Language.

nodes.name: brokenDraft
nodes.summary: brokenDraft is a draft Plan of friday, read from the prompt of req, breaking every structural hard rule: the Rice bowl prepared at dinner is eaten at lunch, before it, and on Saturday, after the Cycle; lasagne fills breakfast a second time; and Portion 999 doesn't exist, leaving the snack empty.

nodes.name: TestCheckPlanReportsEachStructuralHardRule
nodes.summary: check_plan reports every structural hard rule a draft breaks, and refuses one that can't be read before any rule: a Recipe that doesn't exist, a size outside 0.75–1.5.

nodes.name: TestThreeSubmitsBreakingHardRulesFailThePlanningRun
nodes.summary: Three submitted drafts that break a hard rule fail the Run, listing what they broke.

nodes.name: TestAPlanningRunEndingWithoutAPlanProposalFailsWithTheModelsLastMessage
nodes.summary: A planning Run whose model ends without submitting a Plan fails, its last message as the reason.

nodes.name: TestCheckPlansCallsRunOut
nodes.summary: Once its calls are spent, check_plan says to submit the best draft, which submit_plan still stores.

nodes.name: TestASecondPlanningRunIsRefusedWhileOneIsGoingOrAPlanProposalIsPending
nodes.summary: A second planning Run is refused while one is going, and while a Plan Proposal is pending; cancelling a planning Run leaves no Plan Proposal.

nodes.name: TestUsersSeeOnlyTheirOwnPlanProposals
nodes.summary: Two Users never see each other's Plan Proposals, and one's pending Plan Proposal doesn't keep the other from planning.

nodes.name: TestBrowserPlansACycleThroughTheKitchenCheck
nodes.summary: Through a browser: opening a Cycle lands on the Kitchen Check, whose button starts the planning Run on its live Trace, which goes on to the Cycle page and its pending Plan Proposal once the Run ends.

nodes.name: TestCancellingAPlanningRunAfterItsSubmitLeavesNoPlanProposal
nodes.summary: Cancelling a planning Run once its Plan is submitted, as the model sums it up, leaves no Plan Proposal: it is stored only with the Run's success.

nodes.name: TestAPlanProposalThatCantBeStoredFailsItsRun
nodes.summary: A Plan Proposal that can't be stored as its Run ends, its Cycle dropped meanwhile, fails the Run rather than leaving it going.

nodes.name: portions_test.go
nodes.summary: Seam-1 and browser tests for Portions and Lots: adding with validation, grouping alike portions, Italian, isolation, htmx fragments, counting and moving portions, Lot movement history and focus behaviour of sheets.

nodes.name: TestAddedPortionsShowGroupedAboveTheStockItems
nodes.summary: Portions no Prep Session produced are added from the Kitchen page and show as one Lot under their Storage Location, above its Stock Items.

nodes.name: TestAddingPortionsRefusesAMissingValueOnItsField
nodes.summary: Calories, protein, carbs and fat are required, each refused on its field with what was typed kept. Nothing is added.

nodes.name: TestAddingPortionsRefusesNoNameAndNoStorageLocation
nodes.summary: A name and a Storage Location are refused on their fields too, and the page, longer than a screen, opens with a summary linking to each.

nodes.name: TestAddedPortionsShowUnknownFibreAndSugarAsUnknown
nodes.summary: Fibre and sugar may be unknown, and show as unknown: never 0.

nodes.name: TestAddingPortionsTakesAWholeNumberOfAtLeastOne
nodes.summary: How many is a whole number from 1 to 99.

nodes.name: TestPortionsShareALotOnlyWhenAlike
nodes.summary: Alike means the same name, ignoring case and surrounding space, the same values and the same Storage Location: anything else is another Lot.

nodes.name: TestAnAddedPortionFixesTheLanguage
nodes.summary: An added Portion's name is a Food Term, so it fixes the User's Language.

nodes.name: TestAddingPortionsSpeaksItalian
nodes.summary: Portions are told in the User's Language.

nodes.name: TestUsersSeeOnlyTheirOwnPortions
nodes.summary: Two Users never see each other's Portions.

nodes.name: TestAddingPortionsAnswersHTMXWithAFragment
nodes.summary: Posted from the sheet by htmx, an add answers with a fragment: the form as typed when refused, and when added a Notice that closes the sheet and lists the kitchen again.

nodes.name: TestBrowserAddsPortionsInTheSheet
nodes.summary: The chevron only chooses what the + adds, and the + opens that sheet. A refused add comes back in it with focus on the refused field; one accepted closes it, shows the Lot and leaves the choice, which a new page forgets.

nodes.name: TestCountingPortionsUpAddsMoreAlike
nodes.summary: A Count up adds Portions alike, which show with the Lot.

nodes.name: TestCountingPortionsDownRemovesThem
nodes.summary: A Count down removes Portions, and a Count to nothing removes the Lot from the page.

nodes.name: TestCountingPortionsRefusesWhatIsNotACount
nodes.summary: A Count below 0, not a whole number, or above what one Count takes is refused on its field, with what was typed kept and nothing changed.

nodes.name: TestMovingPortions
nodes.summary: Moving some leaves two Lots, and moving all the rest joins it to them, leaving one.

nodes.name: TestMovingPortionsRefusesWhatTheLotCannotGive
nodes.summary: A move above what the Lot holds is refused on its field, and so is a move of none, part of one, or to nowhere.

nodes.name: TestALotsMovementsTellWhyItHoldsWhatItDoes
nodes.summary: A Lot's Movements show newest first, with cause, before and after, and the note; one act is one Movement, and a move tells where it went on the side it left.

nodes.name: TestAPortionCountThatChangesNothingIsAMovement
nodes.summary: A Count that changes nothing is one Movement like any other, and is the Lot's.

nodes.name: TestALotsMovementsBeginWithWhatItHoldsNow
nodes.summary: A Lot emptied and filled again starts its Movements over.

nodes.name: TestALotsMovementsInItalian
nodes.summary: Checks a lots movements in italian.

nodes.name: TestNoLotIsNotFound
nodes.summary: A Portion that isn't the User's, or a place that is no Storage Location, is no Lot.

nodes.name: TestPortionFormsAnswerHTMXWithFragments
nodes.summary: A Count and a move of Portions, posted by htmx, answer with no page: refused, the form as a fragment with what was typed; saved, a Notice for the sheet to close under.

nodes.name: TestBrowserOpensALotsMovementsInPlace
nodes.summary: A Lot's Movements open in the side sheet, leaving the User on the Kitchen page, which a plain URL stands in for without htmx.

nodes.name: TestAddingPortionsRefusesMoreThanALotHolds
nodes.summary: A Portion Lot never holds more than 99: an add that would take it past that is refused on its field, and nothing is added.

nodes.name: TestMovingPortionsRefusesMoreThanALotHolds
nodes.summary: A move that would take the Portion Lot it joins past 99 is refused on its field.

nodes.name: TestAStaleCountToNothingConfirmsNothing
nodes.summary: Posting a Count of nothing from a form another write has overtaken finds nothing to record, so confirms nothing.

nodes.name: TestOnlyASheetOrTheCountSearchFocusesAFieldAsItOpens
nodes.summary: The Add Portions page opens with no field focused, so a phone's keyboard doesn't cover it; each sheet, as it opens, focuses its first field, as the Count page its search.

nodes.name: TestBrowserTheAddPortionsPageRefusedOpensOnItsErrorSummary

nodes.name: spans_test.go
nodes.summary: Seam-1 tests of OpenTelemetry instrumentation using an in-memory span recorder: request, query, beat, Supabase Auth and Run/model-call spans, their attributes, errors and absence of secrets.

nodes.name: recordedSpans
nodes.summary: recordedSpans are the spans the app ended. A request's span ends only once its handler returns, which can be after the client has the response, so GetSpans first waits for every request span begun to end.

nodes.name: withSpans
nodes.summary: withSpans sends the app's spans to the in-memory exporter it returns.

nodes.name: GetSpans
nodes.summary: GetSpans are the spans ended so far, once no request span is still open.

nodes.name: OnStart
nodes.summary: Method of recordedSpans: OnStart helper.

nodes.name: OnEnd
nodes.summary: Method of recordedSpans: OnEnd helper.

nodes.name: TestARequestIsASpanWithItsQueriesUnderIt
nodes.summary: A request is a span named for its route, with a span for each database query it runs under it.

nodes.name: TestTheHealthCheckAndAssetsAreNotSpans
nodes.summary: The container's health check asks every ten seconds, and every page loads the static assets, the service worker and the manifest: their requests are not spans.

nodes.name: TestARequestSpanSaysWhoAndInWhatLanguage
nodes.summary: A signed-in request's span says who the User was, by their id, the Language the page spoke, what the browser asked for, whether htmx sent it, boosted, and which build served it: never their email. Its response gives its trace id.

nodes.name: TestASignedOutRequestSpanHasNoUser
nodes.summary: A request from no one signed in says so, with no User, in the Language the pages were switched to, and not through htmx; one with no Accept-Language records none.

nodes.name: TestARefusalSaysWhyAndIsNoError
nodes.summary: A request the app refuses says why on its span, naming the fields a form refused, and is no error: the User is told why, and nothing went wrong.

nodes.name: TestARefusedRecipeSaysWhy
nodes.summary: A Recipe refused names the fields of its Ingredient rows it refused; one whose new Ingredient is only asked to be confirmed says so, with no field refused.

nodes.name: TestAServerErrorIsAnErrorAndShowsItsTraceID
nodes.summary: A request that fails on the server is an error, and its page gives the trace id to quote in a report.

nodes.name: TestALogLineInARequestSaysWho
nodes.summary: A line the app logs in a signed-in request says whose it was, by their id.

nodes.name: TestABeatIsASpanWithItsQueriesUnderIt
nodes.summary: A scheduler beat is a span, with the queries that bring each User's kitchen up to now under it.

nodes.name: TestRenewingASessionIsASpanUnderTheRequest
nodes.summary: A signed-in request whose session has expired renews it with Supabase Auth: a client span under the request's.

nodes.name: TestFetchingTheJWKSIsASpanUnderTheFirstCheckedRequest
nodes.summary: A fresh server fetches the JWKS from Supabase Auth to check the first access token it sees: a client span under that request's.

nodes.name: TestSupabaseSpansHoldNoSecret
nodes.summary: No span of a call to Supabase Auth holds a secret: the access or refresh tokens, the API key, or the User's email.

nodes.name: TestSupabaseIsSentNoTraceparent
nodes.summary: Supabase Auth is not told the spans' ids: no call to it sends a traceparent header, even with a propagator set for the whole process.

nodes.name: onlySpan
nodes.summary: onlySpan is the one span that matches, described as what; finding none or several fails the test.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: get requests path from the app with header, as a browser or htmx would, returning the response's header.

nodes.name: parseWithSpans
nodes.summary: parseWithSpans is a signed-in User who knows rice, their spans going to the exporter it returns, who has pasted pastedLasagne for a parse Run the model answers with steps.

nodes.name: runAndCallSpans
nodes.summary: runAndCallSpans is the one Run's span among those exported, and the spans of its calls to the model under it, in order.

nodes.name: TestEachCallToTheModelIsASpanUnderItsRun
nodes.summary: Each call a Run makes to the model is a client span under the Run's span, itself under the request that started it: the model, the tokens and why the model stopped, never what it was asked or said. A call that failed is an error span, and so is retried.

nodes.name: TestAFailedRunIsAnErrorSpanAndACancelledOneIsNot

nodes.name: TestARunInterruptedByAStopIsAnErrorSpanButNotItsCall

nodes.name: apptest.go
nodes.summary: Seam-1 test harness that boots Dandori in-process over HTTP against a fresh pgtestdb-cloned Postgres+pgvector database, a Manual clock and FakeAuth, offering HTTP/htmx helpers and raw SQL fixtures.
nodes.languageNotes: Functional options (Option func(*settings)) configure the harness; pgtestdb clones a migrated template database per test so tests run in parallel.

nodes.name: Harness
nodes.summary: Harness is one running app with its own database.

nodes.name: logBuffer
nodes.summary: logBuffer keeps what the app logs, from whichever goroutine logs it.

nodes.name: Response
nodes.summary: Response is a fully read HTTP response.

nodes.name: WithConfig
nodes.summary: WithConfig lets a test change the app's configuration, on top of any earlier change.

nodes.name: WithUnmigratedDatabase
nodes.summary: WithUnmigratedDatabase starts the app on an empty database, as on its first deploy, so the app's own startup applies every migration.

nodes.name: Start
nodes.summary: Start boots the app against a new database cloned from a migrated template, and runs the test in parallel with the others. Everything is torn down when the test ends; a failed test's database is kept for inspection.

nodes.name: Restart
nodes.summary: Restart stops the app and starts it again on the same database, at the same address, as a deploy or a crash and restart does: its Users stay signed in.

nodes.name: Settle
nodes.summary: Settle waits for every Run going to end.

nodes.name: Logged
nodes.summary: Logged is everything the app has logged so far.

nodes.name: Write

nodes.summary: Checks owned appliances are exactly the ticked kinds, with notes collapsed and notes on unticked kinds dropped.

nodes.name: cycle.go
nodes.summary: Models a Cycle (the stretch one supermarket Delivery must last) and its Delivery window: parses an opened Cycle with per-field problems, derives each Cycle's upcoming/current/closed status, lists its Slots and finds which Cycle a Slot belongs to.

nodes.name: Delivery
nodes.summary: One supermarket delivery: its day and time window on that day.

nodes.name: Cycle
nodes.summary: The stretch one Delivery has to last, up to its end date.

nodes.name: Arrives
nodes.summary: When a Delivery is taken to have arrived: the end of its window on its day.

nodes.name: ParseCycle
nodes.summary: Parses a typed Cycle with per-field problems: delivery date/window must be valid and not ended, end date after delivery and within MaxCycleDays, defaulting to DefaultCycleDays.

nodes.name: CycleStatuses
nodes.summary: Derives each Cycle's status at now: upcoming until its Delivery arrives, current until the next one's does, then closed.

nodes.name: Slots
nodes.summary: Lists a Cycle's Slots of every kind each day, from the first after its Delivery arrives to the last on its end date.

nodes.name: CycleOf
nodes.summary: Finds the index of the Cycle a Slot belongs to: arrived before it, not superseded by the next Delivery, and not past its end date.

nodes.name: TestOpeningACycle
nodes.summary: Table test of ParseCycle: valid openings, defaults and each field refusal.

nodes.summary: Checks Cycle statuses move from upcoming to current to closed as Deliveries arrive.

nodes.name: TestACyclesSlots
nodes.summary: Checks a Cycle's Slots start after its Delivery arrives and run to its end date.

nodes.summary: Checks CycleOf assigns Slots to the right Cycle, or none.

nodes.name: TestACycleAcrossAChangeOfTheClocks
nodes.summary: Checks a Cycle's Slots and arrival are correct across a daylight-saving change.

nodes.summary: Writes a TimeOfDay as zero-padded HH:MM.

nodes.name: FormatTime

nodes.name: In

nodes.name: ParseTimeOfDay
nodes.summary: Parses a typed time of day in either form ("13:00", "1pm", "1300") into minutes after midnight, or a problem.

nodes.name: FormatDate

nodes.name: ParseDate

nodes.summary: Checks FormatTime and TimeOfDay.In per Language.

nodes.name: TestATimeIsReadInEitherForm
nodes.summary: Checks ParseTimeOfDay accepts 24-hour and am/pm forms and refuses bad input.

nodes.name: TestADateIsWrittenAndReadTheWayTheLanguageDoes
nodes.summary: Checks FormatDate and ParseDate round-trip in each Language's order.

nodes.name: doc.go
nodes.summary: Package doc for domain: the pure, I/O-free core of Dandori holding the GLOSSARY.md model rules; callers load state, ask the domain, and persist the answer.

nodes.name: foods.go
nodes.summary: Normalises a User's typed list of foods (Profile exclusions or allergies) split on commas, semicolons or newlines, lower-cased, de-duplicated and apostrophe-folded.

nodes.name: NormaliseFoods
nodes.summary: Splits a typed food list on commas, semicolons and newlines, lower-cases, collapses spaces, folds apostrophes and drops blanks and repeats; never nil.

nodes.summary: Seam-2 test that a typed list of foods is normalised into a clean, de-duplicated list.

nodes.name: TestATypedListOfFoodsIsNormalised
nodes.summary: Table test of NormaliseFoods across separators, case, apostrophes and repeats.

nodes.name: ingredient.go
nodes.summary: Core Ingredient model: Units, Storage Locations, Nutrition with optional fibre/sugar Amounts, the shared Problem vocabulary, parsing of typed nutritional values, and the per-Language name normalisation that ignores case, apostrophes and size/grade words.

nodes.name: Ingredient
nodes.summary: A food as the User added it: name, Unit, Nutrition, usual Storage Location and Staple flag.

nodes.name: Nutrition
nodes.summary: Nutritional values: kcal, protein, carbs and fat always known; fibre and sugar may be Unknown.

nodes.name: Amount
nodes.summary: A nutritional value or Unknown (never 0).

nodes.name: Known
nodes.summary: Constructs a known nutritional Amount.

nodes.name: ParseAmount
nodes.summary: Parses a typed nutritional value: blank is Unknown, else non-negative, at most one decimal, below 10000, with point or comma.

nodes.name: Nutrition.Problems
nodes.summary: Reports which of the four always-known nutritional values are missing.

nodes.name: ParseNutrition
nodes.summary: Parses typed nutritional values by field with per-field problems, requiring the four always-known values.

nodes.name: Ingredient.Problems
nodes.summary: Reports what an Ingredient is missing by field: name, unit, usual Storage Location and required nutrition.

nodes.name: NormaliseIngredientName
nodes.summary: Computes the identity key of an Ingredient name in a Language, ignoring case, spacing, typographic apostrophes and size/grade words but keeping plurals.

nodes.name: withoutSizeWords
nodes.summary: Removes a Language's size and grade words (single or multi-word runs) from a name's words, keeping them if nothing else remains.

nodes.name: ingredient_match.go
nodes.summary: Fuzzy matching of Ingredient names: suggests the closest known Ingredient for a mistyped name (exact match, then one-slip edit, then pg_trgm-style trigram similarity) and ranks search results by containment and word-run similarity.
nodes.languageNotes: Reimplements Postgres pg_trgm trigram similarity in pure Go so the domain can rank and suggest names without a database round-trip.

nodes.name: ClosestIngredient
nodes.summary: Suggests the known Ingredient a mistyped name most likely meant: exact normalised match, then one slip away, then trigram similarity above 0.5, ties broken alphabetically.

nodes.name: oneSlipApart
nodes.summary: Reports whether two names differ by one dropped, added or changed letter or one swapped pair of neighbours.

nodes.name: SearchNames
nodes.summary: Returns indices of names a query finds, most alike first: containment or trigram similarity of the whole name or a run of its words above 0.3.

nodes.name: runSimilarity
nodes.summary: Similarity of a query to a name or its most alike run of words, whichever is higher.

nodes.name: trigrams
nodes.summary: Builds the pg_trgm-style set of padded three-letter runs of a string's words.

nodes.name: similarity
nodes.summary: Share of trigrams two sets have in common (Jaccard-style), as pg_trgm computes it.

nodes.name: ingredient_match_test.go
nodes.summary: Seam-2 tests for ClosestIngredient suggestions (near misses, English names, tie-breaking, one-slip edits) and SearchNames ranking.

nodes.name: TestClosestIngredientSuggestsTheKnownIngredientANearMissMeant
nodes.summary: Checks near-miss Italian names suggest the intended known Ingredient and different foods do not.

nodes.name: TestClosestIngredientInEnglish
nodes.summary: Checks suggestions in English, ignoring English size words.

nodes.name: TestClosestIngredientSuggestsANameOneSlipAway
nodes.summary: Checks short names one slip away are suggested.

nodes.name: TestSearchingIngredientsByName
nodes.summary: Checks SearchNames finds and ranks names by containment and typo-tolerant similarity.

nodes.name: ingredient_stress_test.go
nodes.summary: Stress tests the Ingredient name matcher against real kitchen-name lists in English and Italian with generated typos, documenting known limits and checking most names suggest no other.

nodes.name: typosOf
nodes.summary: Generates the one-slip typos of a name (drops, swaps, changes) for stress testing.

nodes.name: TestClosestIngredientFindsRealSlips
nodes.summary: Checks generated slips of real kitchen names suggest the original name.

nodes.name: TestClosestIngredientsKnownLimits
nodes.summary: Documents slips the matcher is known to miss or mis-suggest.

nodes.name: TestSlipsOfKitchenNames
nodes.summary: Measures how often slips of kitchen names are matched back across the name lists.

nodes.name: TestMostKitchenNamesSuggestNoOther
nodes.summary: Checks most real names don't suggest a different known name.

nodes.name: ingredient_test.go
nodes.summary: Seam-2 tests for Ingredient name normalisation (same food alike, different foods apart, size words), amount parsing and the four required nutritional values.

nodes.name: TestIngredientNamesOfOneFoodNormaliseAlike
nodes.summary: Checks variants of one food's name share a normalised key.

nodes.name: TestIngredientNamesOfDifferentFoodsNormaliseApart
nodes.summary: Checks different foods (including plurals) keep different keys.

nodes.name: TestAnAmountIsReadAsTyped
nodes.summary: Table test of ParseAmount values and refusals.

nodes.name: TestAnIngredientNeedsItsFourNutritionalValues
nodes.summary: Checks ParseNutrition requires the four always-known values and allows Unknown fibre/sugar.

nodes.name: language.go
nodes.summary: Defines the User's Language (English or Italian) and the FoodTerms counts that decide whether the Language can still change: only until any Food Term is written (ADR-0015).

nodes.name: FoodTerms
nodes.summary: Counts of Food Terms a User has written per slice (Ingredients, Portions, Recipes, Drafts, Exclusions, Allergies).

nodes.name: ParseLanguage
nodes.summary: Looks up a choosable Language by its ISO 639-1 code.

nodes.name: Any
nodes.summary: Reports whether any Food Term has been written.

nodes.name: LanguageCanChange
nodes.summary: Reports whether a User can still change Language: only before writing any Food Term.

nodes.name: language_test.go
nodes.summary: Seam-2 tests that the Language can change only until a Food Term is written, and that language codes parse.

nodes.name: TestTheLanguageCanChangeUntilAFoodTermIsWritten
nodes.summary: Checks LanguageCanChange flips once any Food Term count is positive.

nodes.name: TestParseLanguage
nodes.summary: Checks valid and invalid language codes.

nodes.name: ledger.go
nodes.summary: The Kitchen Ledger: Quantities in tenths, Movements and their Causes, Stock Items keyed by Ingredient and Storage Location, and the Ledger that adds Movements up to what the kitchen holds at a moment and writes Counts, moves and Portion Movements.
nodes.languageNotes: Quantity is an int64 of tenths so sums are exact, avoiding float rounding drift in an append-only ledger.

nodes.name: StockKey
nodes.summary: Identifies a Stock Item: one Ingredient in one Storage Location.

nodes.name: Movement
nodes.summary: One change to what the kitchen holds: Stock Item, Change, Cause, optional destination, Portions, stated/believed values and note.

nodes.name: StockMovement
nodes.summary: A Movement of one Stock Item with what it held before and after.

nodes.name: StockItem
nodes.summary: What one Ingredient's Movements in one Storage Location add up to.

nodes.name: Ledger
nodes.summary: The Kitchen Ledger: Movements in the order they happened, folded one way so holdings and histories agree.

nodes.name: Number
nodes.summary: Converts a tenths Quantity to a number in its Unit.

nodes.name: QuantityOf
nodes.summary: Converts a number in its Unit to a Quantity of tenths, rounding.

nodes.name: ParseQuantity
nodes.summary: Parses a typed quantity for a Unit: whole grams/millilitres, one decimal for pieces, non-negative and bounded.

nodes.name: Sets
nodes.summary: Reports whether a Cause sets the Stock Item to a stated value (Counted, MarkedStaple).

nodes.name: CheckMove
nodes.summary: Refuses a move of nothing or of more than the Stock Item holds.

nodes.name: ParseCount
nodes.summary: Parses a typed Count of a Stock Item with per-field problems.

nodes.name: ParseMove
nodes.summary: Parses a typed move between two different Storage Locations with per-field problems.

nodes.name: after
nodes.summary: Applies a Movement to a Stock Item's holding, reporting whether it touches that key; Counts set rather than add.

nodes.name: NewLedger
nodes.summary: Constructs a Ledger from Movements in the order they happened.

nodes.name: At
nodes.summary: Folds Movements up to a moment into what the kitchen holds by Stock Item.

nodes.name: PortionsAt
nodes.summary: Folds Movements up to a moment into where each held Portion is.

nodes.name: placePortions
nodes.summary: Updates Portion locations for a Movement: moves relocate, Counts down remove, others place.

nodes.name: HeldAt
nodes.summary: What each Storage Location holds of one Ingredient at a moment.

nodes.name: Movements
nodes.summary: Every Movement touching a Stock Item with its before/after holdings, showing what Counts believed.

nodes.name: WriteAt
nodes.summary: Picks when a new Movement happens: now, or the last Movement's time if later, so it always comes after the Ledger.

nodes.name: Count
nodes.summary: Builds a Count Movement of the difference between stated and believed, keeping both.

nodes.name: AddPortions
nodes.summary: Builds the one Movement adding new Portions to a Storage Location.

nodes.name: CountPortions
nodes.summary: Builds a Count Movement of a Portion Lot, listing Portions added or the ones taken (unslotted oldest first).

nodes.name: MovePortions
nodes.summary: Builds a move of the oldest Portions of a Lot to another Lot, refused when CheckMove or the target's capacity says no.

nodes.name: LotMovements
nodes.summary: A Portion Lot's Movements with before/after counts, since its oldest held Portion arrived.

nodes.name: Move
nodes.summary: Builds a move of a quantity from one Stock Item to another Storage Location, refused by CheckMove.

nodes.name: CountToNothing
nodes.summary: Builds the Counts to nothing for each Stock Item of an Ingredient being marked a Staple.

nodes.name: ledger_test.go
nodes.summary: Seam-2 tests for quantity parsing, move checks, the Ledger's holdings at a moment, moves between Stock Items, Counts that stand, a Stock Item's Movement history and writing Movements.

nodes.name: TestParseQuantity
nodes.summary: Table test of ParseQuantity per Unit and decimal mark.

nodes.name: TestAQuantityIsANumber
nodes.summary: Checks Quantity and number conversions round-trip exactly.

nodes.name: TestCheckMove
nodes.summary: Checks CheckMove refusals.

nodes.name: lastLinesAgree
nodes.summary: Helper asserting a Stock Item's last Movement line agrees with the Ledger's holding.

nodes.name: TestTheLedgerAddsUpToAMoment
nodes.summary: Checks Ledger.At sums Movements up to and including a moment.

nodes.name: TestAMoveTakesFromOneStockItemAndGivesToAnother
nodes.summary: Checks a move debits one Stock Item and credits another.

nodes.name: TestACountStands
nodes.summary: Checks a Count sets the holding regardless of earlier Movements.

nodes.name: TestAStockItemsMovements
nodes.summary: Checks a Stock Item's Movement history with before/after values.

nodes.name: TestTheLedgerWritesAMovement
nodes.summary: Checks Count, Move and WriteAt build correct Movements and timestamps.

nodes.name: TestParseCount
nodes.summary: Checks ParseCount values and refusals.

nodes.name: TestParseMove
nodes.summary: Checks ParseMove values and refusals.

nodes.name: meal_out.go

nodes.name: MealOutRequired
nodes.summary: Reports whether a Meal Out field is required (all but fibre and sugar).

nodes.name: ParseMealOut
nodes.summary: Parses the typed Meal Out estimate into Nutrition with per-field problems.

nodes.name: meal_out_test.go
nodes.summary: Seam-2 table test for parsing the Meal Out estimate, its required and optional fields and its refusals.

nodes.name: TestParseMealOut
nodes.summary: Table test of ParseMealOut values, Unknown optionals and refusals.

nodes.name: plan.go
nodes.summary: Plan model for a Cycle: Prep Sessions with the Portions they yield, Portions kept into Slots, ingredient scaling and per-Portion nutrition, Slot ordering/equality, readability checks and the structural hard rules (slot filled twice, empty slot, eaten before prepared, unknown portion, outside cycle).

nodes.name: Plan
nodes.summary: A Cycle's Plan: Prep Sessions and the unslotted Portions it keeps into Slots.

nodes.name: PrepSession
nodes.summary: One preparation at a Slot of a Recipe at a size, or an Ingredient as is, with the Portions it yields.

nodes.name: PlannedPortion
nodes.summary: A Portion a Prep Session yields: where it is kept and the Slot it is eaten at, if any.

nodes.name: Kept
nodes.summary: Assigns an existing unslotted Portion to a Slot.

nodes.name: Violation
nodes.summary: A hard rule a Plan breaks and where, as text for the planner.

nodes.name: Name
nodes.summary: What a Prep Session prepares: its Recipe's or Ingredient's name.

nodes.name: Ingredients
nodes.summary: A Prep Session's ingredient quantities: the Recipe's scaled by portions and size, or the Ingredient per Portion, pieces rounded to at least one.

nodes.name: NutritionPerPortion
nodes.summary: One planned Portion's nutrition: the Recipe's per-Portion scaled by size, or the Ingredient at its quantity.

nodes.name: Before
nodes.summary: Orders Slots by day then kind.

nodes.name: Slot.String
nodes.summary: Writes a Slot for the planner, e.g. "dinner on Thu 5 Nov".

nodes.name: Equal
nodes.summary: Slot equality by day and kind, independent of time zone.

nodes.name: Unreadable
nodes.summary: Lists why a draft Plan can't be read: Portion size outside 0.75-1.5, a Prep Session yielding nothing, an unslotted Portion kept twice.

nodes.name: Violation.String
nodes.summary: Writes a Violation as "rule: message".

nodes.name: HardRules
nodes.summary: Checks a Plan against the structural hard rules over the planned Slots: each filled once, none empty, nothing eaten before prepared, only known unslotted Portions, nothing outside the Cycle.

nodes.name: plan_test.go
nodes.summary: Seam-2 tests for scaling a Prep Session's ingredients, Portion nutrition by size, unreadable draft Plans, the structural hard rules and Slot equality by day and kind.

nodes.name: TestAPrepSessionScalesItsIngredients
nodes.summary: Checks Prep Session ingredient scaling by portions and size, rounding pieces.

nodes.name: TestAPortionsNutritionScalesWithItsSize
nodes.summary: Checks per-Portion nutrition scales with size.

nodes.name: TestADraftPlanThatCantBeRead
nodes.summary: Checks Unreadable reports bad sizes, empty sessions and double-kept Portions.

nodes.name: TestTheStructuralHardRules
nodes.summary: Table test of each structural hard rule violation.

nodes.name: TestSlotsAreEqualByDayAndKind
nodes.summary: Checks Slot equality ignores time zone and ordering.

nodes.name: portion.go
nodes.summary: Portion model: ready-to-eat servings, parsing typed Portions and counts, Portion Lots grouping alike Portions by name, nutrition and Storage Location, capacity checks and which Portions a Count down takes.

nodes.name: Portion
nodes.summary: One ready-to-eat serving with per-Portion values; location comes from its Movements (ADR-0013).

nodes.name: NewPortions
nodes.summary: Portions a User adds directly, not from a Prep Session.

nodes.name: TypedPortions
nodes.summary: Portions as typed in a form, nutrition by field.

nodes.name: PortionLot
nodes.summary: Alike held Portions: same normalised name, nutrition and Storage Location.

nodes.name: LotKey
nodes.summary: Identifies a Portion Lot by one alike Portion and a Storage Location.

nodes.name: ParsePortions
nodes.summary: Parses typed Portions with per-field problems: name, how many, location and required nutrition.

nodes.name: ParseHowMany
nodes.summary: Parses how many Portions to add: a whole number from 1 to 99.

nodes.name: Count
nodes.summary: How many Portions a Lot holds.

nodes.name: CheckFits
nodes.summary: Refuses more Portions joining a Lot past the 99 cap.

nodes.name: MoreAlike
nodes.summary: The new alike Portions a Count above the Lot's holding adds.

nodes.name: takes
nodes.summary: Picks which Portions a Count down removes: unslotted oldest first, then latest Slot.

nodes.name: ParsePortionCount
nodes.summary: Parses a typed Count of a Portion Lot as a whole number up to the cap.

nodes.name: LotOf
nodes.summary: Finds the Portion Lot a LotKey names, empty if its location holds none.

nodes.name: LotLike
nodes.summary: Builds the Lot alike a Portion in a location from the held Portions.

nodes.name: PortionLots
nodes.summary: Groups held Portions into Lots by Storage Location then name.

nodes.name: portion_test.go
nodes.summary: Seam-2 tests for Portion parsing, grouping into Lots, following their Movements, counting up and down, moving Portions, Lot Movement history and the 99-Portion Lot cap.

nodes.name: TestParseHowMany
nodes.summary: Checks ParseHowMany bounds.

nodes.name: TestPortionLots
nodes.summary: Checks Portions group into Lots by location, name and nutrition.

nodes.name: TestAddingPortionsIsOneMovement
nodes.summary: Checks AddPortions builds a single Movement.

nodes.name: TestParsePortions
nodes.summary: Checks ParsePortions values and refusals.

nodes.name: TestPortionsFollowTheirMovements
nodes.summary: Checks PortionsAt follows adds, moves and Counts.

nodes.name: TestLotOf
nodes.summary: Checks LotOf finds or empties a Lot.

nodes.name: TestParsePortionCount
nodes.summary: Checks ParsePortionCount values and refusals.

nodes.name: TestCountingPortions
nodes.summary: Checks CountPortions up, down and unchanged, and which Portions are taken.

nodes.name: TestMovingPortions
nodes.summary: Checks MovePortions moves the oldest and refuses overflows.

nodes.name: TestLotMovements
nodes.summary: Checks a Lot's Movement history.

nodes.name: TestAPortionLotHoldsAtMost99
nodes.summary: Checks the 99-Portion cap on Lots.

nodes.name: Profile
nodes.summary: A User's stored settings: Language, Slot times, Targets, Meal Out, exclusions, allergies, appliances.

nodes.summary: A Quantity of an Ingredient in a Recipe.

nodes.summary: A reusable dish: name, portions, minutes, Slot kinds, appliances, steps and Ingredients.

nodes.summary: One Portion's nutrition, with floors for fibre and sugar when some Ingredients don't know them.

nodes.summary: Unique key of a Recipe name: lower-cased and trimmed.

nodes.summary: Validates a Recipe by field and each Ingredient row: required fields, active within total minutes, new Ingredients complete, no Ingredient listed twice, positive quantities.

nodes.summary: Checks that recipe nutrition per portion is derived from its ingredients.

nodes.name: TestRecipeNutritionPerPortionFloorsFibreAndSugarApart
nodes.summary: Test: Fibre and sugar are each their own floor.

nodes.summary: Tests recipe validation.

nodes.summary: Tests parse minutes.

nodes.summary: Test: Two names that differ only by case and surrounding space are one Recipe's name.

nodes.summary: Today is the day's Slots as Today shows them at a moment.

nodes.name: Before
nodes.summary: Before is the kind before k in the day; breakfast has none, "".

nodes.name: TestASlotIsAtItsTimeOfDayOnTheWallClock
nodes.summary: Test: A Slot's time of day is on the wall clock, on a day the clocks go back as on any other.

nodes.name: ByField

nodes.name: target_test.go

nodes.name: Date
nodes.summary: Date is day's weekday and date in the Language of ctx: "Monday, November 2", "lunedì 2 novembre".

nodes.name: ShortDate
nodes.summary: ShortDate is Date for a line with little room: "Mon, Nov 2", "Lun 2 Nov".

nodes.name: ShortDateInYear

nodes.name: DateTime
nodes.summary: DateTime is when at was, as of now: its ShortDate, with its year unless that is now's, and its Time, apart so the day doesn't run into the hour: "Mon, Nov 2 · 9:00 am", "Lun 2 Nov · 09:00".

nodes.name: Time
nodes.summary: Time is the time of day of at in the Language of ctx: "13:00" in Italian, "1:00 pm" in English.

nodes.name: Capitalised
nodes.summary: Capitalised is s with its first letter a capital, as a name starting a label is.

nodes.name: Number
nodes.summary: Number is v as the request's Language writes it, a decimal comma in Italian.

nodes.name: 00001_enable_pgvector.sql
nodes.summary: Goose migration enabling the pgvector extension in PostgreSQL, laying the groundwork for vector-similarity features.

nodes.name: 00002_users.sql
nodes.summary: Creates the Supabase-style `authenticated` role, the current_user_id() helper reading the JWT sub claim, and the row-level-secured user table that establishes the own_rows policy pattern every owned table follows.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses goose StatementBegin/End around a PL/pgSQL DO block so the role creation tolerates an already-existing Supabase role; RLS policies wrap current_user_id() in a sub-SELECT so Postgres evaluates it once per query.

nodes.name: 00003_profile.sql
nodes.summary: Creates the profile table, the first User-owned table, holding the User's chosen Language (en/it) under row-level security.

nodes.name: 00004_kitchen.sql
nodes.summary: Creates the kitchen table recording how far each User's kitchen has been brought up to now (up_to) and the scheduler's last beat (beaten_at), per ADR-0013.

nodes.name: 00005_slot_times.sql
nodes.summary: Adds the four meal Slot times (breakfast, lunch, snack, dinner) to profile, constrained to be all-or-none and in daily order.

nodes.name: 00006_ingredient.sql
nodes.summary: Creates the ingredient table: a User's hand-added foods with a normalised unique name, unit, per-unit nutrition values, storage location and staple flag.

nodes.name: 00007_movement.sql
nodes.summary: Creates the append-only movement table, the Kitchen Ledger (ADR-0013), where Stock Items are derived by summing signed changes; Counts record believed vs stated quantities.

nodes.name: 00008_move.sql
nodes.summary: Extends movement with a moved_to column and a 'moved' cause kind so moving stock between Storage Locations is a single ledger event.

nodes.name: 00009_ingredient_edit.sql
nodes.summary: Grants the authenticated role UPDATE and DELETE on ingredient so Users can edit and delete Ingredients, still restricted by movement's deferred foreign key.

nodes.name: 00010_staple.sql
nodes.summary: Adds the 'staple' movement cause: marking an Ingredient a Staple counts its Stock Items to zero, enforced by a CHECK constraint.

nodes.name: 00011_portion.sql
nodes.summary: Creates the portion table for ready-to-eat servings and the movement_portion join table, and extends movement with an 'added' cause so a Movement can concern a set of Portions instead of an Ingredient.

nodes.name: 00012_recipe.sql
nodes.summary: Creates the recipe table (portions, timings, slot kinds, appliances, steps) and the ordered recipe_ingredient table linking Recipes to the User's Ingredients with quantities.

nodes.name: 00013_recipe_edit.sql
nodes.summary: Grants UPDATE/DELETE on recipe and DELETE on recipe_ingredient so Users can edit and delete Recipes, an edit replacing Ingredient rows.

nodes.name: 00014_run.sql
nodes.summary: Creates the run table for a User's agent Runs, the trace_event table storing each Run's Trace as kind-plus-jsonb events, and recipe_draft holding a parsed Recipe document produced by a Run.

nodes.name: 00015_recipe_draft_delete.sql
nodes.summary: Grants DELETE on recipe_draft so accepting or discarding a Recipe Draft removes it.

nodes.name: 00016_targets.sql
nodes.summary: Adds the daily nutrition Targets (kcal, protein, fibre, sugar; all-or-none) and a calorie tolerance percentage to profile.

nodes.name: 00017_appliance_kinds.sql
nodes.summary: Constrains recipe.appliances to the fixed list of appliance kinds defined by ADR-0020.

nodes.name: 00018_meal_out.sql
nodes.summary: Adds the Meal Out nutrition estimate columns with defaults to profile, used when a Meal Out Exception gives no values of its own.

nodes.name: 00019_exclusions_and_brief.sql
nodes.summary: Adds food exclusions, allergies and the free-text Planning Brief to profile, all starting empty.

nodes.name: 00020_profile_appliances.sql
nodes.summary: Adds a jsonb appliances map to profile keyed by ADR-0020 appliance kinds with optional model notes, defaulting to a hob and an oven.

nodes.name: 00021_cycle.sql
nodes.summary: Creates the cycle table holding each User's Cycles with Delivery date, delivery time window and end date (at most 14 days on); status is derived, not stored.

nodes.name: 00022_plan_proposal.sql
nodes.summary: Creates the planning schema: cycle_run linking a planning Run to its Cycle and first Slot, plan_proposal (at most one pending per User), prep_session, planned_portion and kept_portion, all under row-level security.
nodes.languageNotes: Composite (user_id, id) foreign keys keep every reference within one User's rows, and a partial unique index (WHERE status = 'pending') enforces at most one pending Plan Proposal.

nodes.name: user
nodes.summary: A User, created at first sign-in and keyed by their Supabase Auth id; owns itself under the own_rows RLS policy.

nodes.name: profile
nodes.summary: A User's Profile: Language, later extended with slot times, targets, Meal Out estimate, exclusions, Planning Brief and appliances.

nodes.name: kitchen
nodes.summary: Per-User kitchen clock: the moment the kitchen was last brought up to and the scheduler's last beat.

nodes.name: ingredient
nodes.summary: A User's Ingredient with normalised unique name, unit, nutrition per unit, storage location and staple flag.

nodes.name: movement
nodes.summary: Append-only Kitchen Ledger entry: a signed change to an Ingredient (or Portions) at a Storage Location with its cause.

nodes.name: portion
nodes.summary: A ready-to-eat serving with per-Portion nutrition; its location and status derive from its Movements.

nodes.name: movement_portion
nodes.summary: Append-only join listing the Portions a Movement concerns, with deferred foreign keys.

nodes.name: recipe
nodes.summary: A User's Recipe with normalised name, portion count, timings, slot kinds, appliances and steps.

nodes.name: recipe_ingredient
nodes.summary: Ordered list of a Recipe's Ingredients with quantities, each Ingredient at most once.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: A User's agent Run with kind, status (going/succeeded/failed/cancelled), what it was asked and its timing.

nodes.name: trace_event
nodes.summary: A sequenced Trace Event of a Run: a kind plus jsonb data, never fixed prose.

nodes.name: recipe_draft
nodes.summary: A parsed Recipe document (jsonb) produced by a Run, awaiting acceptance or discard.

nodes.name: cycle
nodes.summary: A User's Cycle: Delivery date and time window plus end date, with status derived from the clock.

nodes.name: cycle_run
nodes.summary: Links a planning Run to the Cycle it plans and the first Slot (day and kind) it plans from.

nodes.name: plan_proposal
nodes.summary: The Plan Proposal a planning Run stored, with summary and status; a partial unique index allows at most one pending per User.

nodes.name: prep_session
nodes.summary: A Plan Proposal's Prep Session at a Slot, preparing either a Recipe at a size or an Ingredient as-is with a per-Portion quantity.

nodes.name: planned_portion
nodes.summary: The ordered Portions a Prep Session yields, with storage location and optional eating Slot.

nodes.name: kept_portion
nodes.summary: Existing unslotted Portions a Plan Proposal assigns to eating Slots.

nodes.name: 0005-cart-fill-never-checks-out.md
nodes.summary: ADR stating Cart Fill stops at the online supermarket cart and never automates checkout or payment, protecting the user's money and store account.

nodes.name: 0011-stock-items-have-no-expiry-date.md

nodes.name: 0016-cart-fill-runs-in-a-browser-extension.md
