layers.description: Project vision, glossary, README, agent instructions and guides, the design system and the ADRs that record architectural decisions.

tour.title: What Dandori Is
tour.description: Start with the README, which frames Dandori as a batch-cooking meal-planning co-pilot: cook once and eat three times, plan one grocery delivery (a Cycle) at a time, let Today tell you what to do, and have the agent propose changes you approve. The vision document walks through a Cycle week by week and lays out the M1/M2 roadmap, while GLOSSARY.md defines the ubiquitous language (Cycle, Slot, Portion, Plan Proposal, Kitchen Ledger) that every later step and every type name relies on.

tour.title: The Single Binary Entry
tour.description: cmd/dandori/main.go is the only entry point: its serve command reads DANDORI_* and Anthropic settings from the environment, wires telemetry, picks the real Claude client or a demo LLM, connects Supabase auth and serves HTTP with graceful shutdown. It has one of the highest fan-outs in the graph, so reading it gives you a map of every runtime dependency before you dive into any one of them.
tour.languageLesson: Go programs start in package main's func main. Graceful shutdown is typically done with signal.NotifyContext and http.Server.Shutdown, which lets in-flight requests finish before the process exits.

tour.title: Composition Root and Tiers
tour.description: internal/app/app.go is the composition root, with the highest fan-out of any file: it opens and migrates the database, constructs every feature Service (auth, profile, ingredients, ledger, runs, recipes, kitchen, planning, today) and registers all HTTP routes. ADR-0006 explains why code is grouped by feature, each with web_ handlers, a Service and a store, and .golangci.yml enforces the resulting one-way dependencies with depguard: domain, agent, db and web are leaves, only app wires features, and Today sits at the top.
tour.languageLesson: Go has no dependency-injection framework by convention; a composition root that calls constructors explicitly keeps wiring visible. Lint rules like depguard turn an architectural rule ("domain must not import db") into a build failure.

tour.title: The Pure Domain Core
tour.description: internal/domain is the most depended-upon package in the codebase: its files top the fan-in ranking because every feature asks it for rules. doc.go states the contract, a pure I/O-free core where callers load state, ask the domain and persist the answer. Cycle models the stretch one Delivery must last, Slots are the eating times of a day, Portions are ready-to-eat servings, and Plan ties them together through Prep Sessions and structural hard rules, all named exactly as in the Glossary from Step 1.
tour.languageLesson: A functional core with an imperative shell keeps Go domain code free of context.Context, database handles and clocks; time is passed in as a value, so tests (Seam-2) need no mocks.

tour.title: Database and Row Security
tour.description: The domain from Step 4 is persisted in PostgreSQL with pgvector on Supabase. db.go opens a traced pgx pool, applies the embedded goose migrations and defines the Querier interface every store uses to join a caller's transaction; user.go runs each request's work as Supabase's authenticated role with the User's JWT claims. Migration 00002 creates that role, the current_user_id() helper and the own_rows row-level-security policy that every owned table follows, so Users share nothing at the database level.
tour.languageLesson: PostgreSQL row-level security attaches a policy (for example user_id = current_user_id()) to a table, so every query is filtered by the database itself, even one a developer forgot to scope. Goose migrations are numbered SQL files applied in order and recorded in a version table.

tour.title: The Kitchen Ledger
tour.description: What is in the kitchen is not stored as mutable stock: per ADR-0013 it is an append-only ledger of Movements, and stock and Portions are computed by adding them up. domain/ledger.go holds that arithmetic, while the ledger package's Service is the write gateway that locks a User's kitchen, saves Movements and brings every kitchen up to now on requests and on the scheduler beat. ADR-0019 explains why the ledger moved into its own package below the features that write Movements, removing a dependency cycle in the tiers from Step 3.

tour.title: Anatomy of a Feature
tour.description: The kitchen feature shows the ADR-0006 slice in practice. Its web_handlers bring the ledger up to now before each page and serve the counting, moving and adding sheets; its Service computes Stock Items and Portion Lots from the Ledger in Step 6 and records changes inside transactions holding the kitchen lock. tiers_test.go is the guardrail that keeps every feature honest: only web_ files may import the web package, and only store files may touch the database.

tour.title: Web Shell and Design
tour.description: Every feature page is built from the shared web package using Go, templ and htmx. answer.go defines Answer, the uniform reply to a write (ADR-0009): a fragment plus a floating Notice for htmx, or a redirect for a plain browser, so forms work with and without JavaScript. i18n.go carries the User's Language (English or Italian) through the request, and docs/design.md with app.css define the Pixel ledger design system's tokens and components.
tour.languageLesson: htmx lets plain HTML attributes issue requests and swap server-rendered fragments into the page. Returning either a fragment or a full redirect from the same handler (progressive enhancement) keeps the app usable when htmx is not loaded.

tour.title: The Hand-Rolled Agent
tour.description: Instead of an agent framework, ADR-0003 chose a hand-written tool-use loop. agent.go defines the LLM port and message vocabulary, brief.go the Brief a Run is given (system prompt, user prompt, effort, tools), and loop.go sends it to the model, runs requested tools, retries retryable failures with backoff and emits every step as a Trace Event. The anthropic adapter implements the port over Claude's Messages API with prompt caching, so the engine itself stays provider-independent.
tour.languageLesson: In Go, a small interface (a port) such as an LLM with one method lets you swap the real Claude adapter for a scripted fake in tests; interfaces are satisfied implicitly, so the adapter never names the interface it implements.

tour.title: Runs and Live Traces
tour.description: The runs feature turns the agent loop from Step 9 into something a User can watch: its Engine starts Runs in the background as their User, records each Run and its Trace Events, supports cancel and follow, and fails Runs a crash left going. Its handlers stream Trace Events live as server-sent events, which is how the README's promise that every agent run has a live trace is delivered. Recipe parsing is the simplest Run kind, turning pasted text into a Recipe Draft through a submit_recipe tool.

tour.title: Planning a Cycle
tour.description: Planning brings everything together. The planning Service opens and drops Cycles, and service_plan.go starts a planning Run whose prompt is built from the Profile, the Recipe Library and the kitchen contents, exposing check_plan and submit_plan tools that validate drafts against the domain Plan rules from Step 4. The result is a pending Plan Proposal, never an applied plan, matching the idea that the agent proposes and you approve; migration 00022 stores it with its Prep Sessions and planned Portions.
tour.languageLesson: A partial unique index (UNIQUE ... WHERE status = 'pending') enforces 'at most one pending Plan Proposal per User' in the database while still allowing any number of accepted or rejected ones.

tour.title: Today and the Clock
tour.description: Today is the top of the tier stack: its Service composes the Profile's Slot times, the kitchen's last beat and the current Cycle into the Day a User sees on opening Dandori. All of it hinges on clock.go, the single place the app reads the time, with a real Clock that beats on a ticker (driving the ledger's bring-up-to-now) and a Manual clock that tests can move forward deterministically.

tour.title: Testing at Two Seams
tour.description: testing.md describes the strategy: Seam-1 drives the whole app over HTTP and in a browser, Seam-2 tests the pure domain. apptest.go boots Dandori in-process against a freshly cloned Postgres database with the Manual clock from Step 12 and a fake Supabase Auth, scenario.go adds a Given/When/Then DSL acting as the User, and fakellm scripts model replies so agent Runs are deterministic. planning_test.go shows them combined to test the planner end to end.

tour.title: Build, Ship and Observe
tour.description: mise.toml pins the toolchain and defines the tasks (dev, test, check, guardrails) CI runs. The two-stage Dockerfile compiles one static binary and runs it on a distroless nonroot image, deploy/compose.yaml runs it behind Caddy on a Hetzner VPS, and the GitHub Actions workflow checks templ drift and the full suite before deploying. telemetry.go exports spans and logs over OTLP to Grafana Cloud, which is how a production request or Run is investigated.
tour.languageLesson: Multi-stage Docker builds compile in a full Go image and copy only the binary into a minimal runtime image; a distroless nonroot base has no shell or package manager, shrinking both image size and attack surface.
